units.name: People and environment issues – making geographical decisions
units.blurb: People and environment issues – making geographical decisions

topics.name: People and environment issues – making geographical decisions

connections.why: Tectonic and climatic hazards have far greater impacts in less-developed countries
Economic development drives the rapid urbanisation of emerging-economy cities
Many fast-growing cities sit in hazard-prone zones, raising disaster risk
Climate and weather processes also reshape UK coasts and river landscapes
Physical landscapes set the stage on which the UK's human geography develops
Both examine how urbanisation and economic change reshape settlements
Global development patterns provide context for UK economic and population change
Coastal and river landscapes are common UK physical fieldwork enquiries
Urban regeneration and change are common UK human fieldwork enquiries
Climate and resource pressures feed the decision-making issues of Paper 3
Development trade-offs are central to the geographical decisions examined
Managing urban growth sustainably is a key decision-making theme
